capabilities.title: Factor 1: Natural Language to Tool Calls
capabilities.sourceEvidence: The current guide describes an LLM selecting a structured tool call while deterministic software executes it.
capabilities.reason: The active Nexus agent catalog exposes named JSON-schema tool calls and provider loops execute only those fixed tools; free-form model text never becomes executable code.

capabilities.title: Factor 2: Own your prompts
capabilities.sourceEvidence: The current guide's Factor 2 requires product code to own prompt construction rather than surrendering it to a framework.
capabilities.reason: Nexus owns provider-neutral prompt construction, system authority, role prompts, and live-context composition in tracked project modules.

capabilities.title: Factor 3: Own your context window
capabilities.sourceEvidence: The current guide treats context engineering and explicit context ownership as a production responsibility.
capabilities.reason: Every active provider path now receives a deterministic 64,000-character ceiling with separate system/message budgets, per-message bounds, newest-message preservation, and explicit omission receipts.

capabilities.title: Factor 4: Tools are just structured outputs
capabilities.sourceEvidence: The current guide models tool calls as structured model output that deterministic code can validate and execute.
capabilities.reason: Every model-produced tool payload is checked against the selected tool's declared schema subset before browser, memory, approval, draft, or protected server handling; unknown tools/fields, missing requirements, wrong types, oversized strings, and malformed arrays fail closed.

capabilities.title: Factor 5: Unify execution state and business state
capabilities.sourceEvidence: The current guide asks applications to represent workflow and domain state together instead of splitting opaque framework state from product state.
capabilities.reason: The reducer tracks objective size, context posture, phase, iteration, tools, human waits, and terminal state; its metadata-only summary is stored on the existing Nexus run artifact beside verification and continuity business evidence.

capabilities.title: Factor 6: Launch/Pause/Resume with simple APIs
capabilities.sourceEvidence: The current guide's Factor 6 calls for explicit launch, pause, and resume transitions instead of a hidden uninterruptible loop.
capabilities.reason: Nexus now has pure launch/human-wait/resume transitions, while the active proposed-edit gate pauses irreversible work and existing unfinished-session continuity provides explicit durable re-entry.

capabilities.title: Factor 7: Contact humans with tool calls
capabilities.sourceEvidence: The current guide treats human contact as a typed tool step rather than an out-of-band framework exception.
capabilities.reason: The typed propose_project_edit call creates visible pending state and requires operator approval before mutation; the reducer records a metadata-only human-wait event without storing the proposal payload.

capabilities.title: Factor 8: Own your control flow
capabilities.sourceEvidence: The current guide places loops, branches, retries, fallbacks, and stopping decisions in product-owned deterministic software.
capabilities.reason: Nexus owns provider loops, iteration ceilings, tool dispatch, rate-limit fallback, local/cloud policy, verification, and terminal handling in TypeScript instead of importing an agent framework.

capabilities.title: Factor 9: Compact Errors into Context Window
capabilities.sourceEvidence: The current guide requires large failures and tool results to be compacted before they consume later model context.
capabilities.reason: Operator-visible tool results remain intact, while every provider conversation receives an 8,000-character head/tail result with an explicit omitted-character receipt.

capabilities.title: Factor 10: Small, Focused Agents
capabilities.sourceEvidence: The current guide recommends narrow agents with focused responsibilities instead of one universal prompt/tool surface.
capabilities.reason: Nexus keeps five named roles with bounded role prompts and selects intent-scoped tool packs rather than exposing the full catalog to every run.

capabilities.title: Factor 11: Trigger from anywhere, meet users where they are
capabilities.sourceEvidence: The current guide combines event-source flexibility with delivery through the product surfaces users already occupy.
capabilities.reason: Within Nexus's supported boundary, runs can begin from the HQ UI, protected HTTP/runtime routes, and approved scheduled missions and are delivered through the web/Tauri product plus durable VAULT/notification/review targets. Unconnected Slack, email, Telegram, and arbitrary webhooks remain unavailable rather than being implied.

capabilities.title: Factor 12: Make your agent a stateless reducer
capabilities.sourceEvidence: The current guide defines the agent transition as current state plus event producing a new state.
capabilities.reason: Nexus execution transitions are now a pure immutable reducer with caller-supplied time, bounded events, explicit terminal states, and a content-free summary; runtime fixtures prove that prior state is unchanged.
